Alirocumab versus placebo: percent change in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo?

https://clinicaltrials.gov/		Every included trial's posted results were retrieved from the registry API and read field by field. Each contributes a least-squares mean difference with a 95 per cent interval from the trial's own analysis; no effect was reconstructed.

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24

Pooled result

MD -54.72 (-60.62 to -48.82), 95% interval

Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24. random, estimator REML, k = 8.

τ² 61.44 · I² 90.02% · Q 58.42 on 7 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

high

Every included trial reports this outcome with an effect estimate and an interval.

How to read this: Between-trial variation is high: I-squared is 90.0 per cent and tau-squared 61.44 under REML. The trials differ in background statin therapy, in population, and in dose regimen, so the pooled figure summarises a range of settings rather than estimating one common effect. Heterogeneity was already high at k=6 (I-squared 87.9) and the recovery did not create it.

Prediction interval -71.18 to -38.26

THIS IS THE NUMBER TO QUOTE, and it is not the headline. The confidence interval -60.62 to -48.82 is about where the AVERAGE lies. The prediction interval -71.18 to -38.26 is about where the effect in a NEW trial of this drug would lie, and it is over three times wider. The eight trials range from -39.1 to -64.1 with tight intervals of their own, so the spread is real and not sampling noise: dose regimen differs, as do population and background statin therapy. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a 25-point range. [RESTATED 2026-08-20: this paragraph quoted the confidence interval and the prediction interval TO ONE DECIMAL, and the number guard on this pass generates two-, three- and four-decimal forms only, so a one-decimal quotation walks past it. Widening the guard to one decimal would fire on most sentences in the corpus; this is restated by hand instead, and the gap is named rather than closed. Found on the rendered page after both guards passed.]

What other estimators give on the same values

Table 6. What other estimators give on the same values
Estimatorτ²I²Pooled (95%)
DerSimonian-Laird50.0488%-54.82 (-60.23 to -49.42)
REML (as displayed)61.4490%-54.72 (-60.62 to -48.82)
REML with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman
t_7 = 2.3646, not a normal quantile		61.4490%-54.72 (-62.06 to -47.38)

The point estimate barely moves -- 54.8 against 54.7 percent -- and no reading of the direction or the magnitude changes. THE INTERVAL MOVES: 10.8 points wide under DerSimonian-Laird, 11.8 under REML, 14.7 under REML with Hartung-Knapp. A reader who wants the most conservative statement of what eight trials establish should take the last of those.

I-SQUARED SITS EXACTLY ON THE THRESHOLD, AND WHICH SIDE DEPENDS ON THE DEFINITION AS WELL AS THE ESTIMATOR. 88.0 per cent under DerSimonian-Laird and 90.0 under REML on metafor's definition; 88.0 under BOTH on Higgins's. This project's poolability screen treats 90 per cent as the point at which an average conceals more than it conveys, so at k=8 the verdict on whether these eight trials should be averaged at all lands ON the line rather than clearly either side of it. At k=6 the REML figure was 91.6 and clearly across. THE RECOVERY MOVED THIS TOWARD POOLABILITY, which is the opposite direction from the one that would flatter a decision already taken, and is stated for that reason.

Comparison with published syntheses

Eight trials, one endpoint, and every value posted by the registry -- so the trial-by-trial check here is complete in a way it cannot be where trials post no results. It is also the topic where the error found is OURS, and it is in the table below with the same weight as anything found in the literature.

12 checks were applied and 8 came back clean, 1 found an error, 1 found something absent and 2 could not be settled at the layer available. The denominator is stated because a list of only the failures is not a finding, it is a selection.

Confirmations are listed in the same table, in the same detail, as errors. Across the cardiology topics reconciled so far the published literature has been implicated in none of them: where a defect existed it was ours. A comparison with room only for their errors could not have found that out.

The syntheses reconciled against

Table 12. The syntheses reconciled against
34754882A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Therapeutic Efficacy and Safety of Alirocumab and Evolocumab on Familial Hypercholesterolemia. Biomed Res Int 2022.
It pools BOTH drugs and restricts to familial hypercholesterolaemia; we pool one drug across a mixed population. Its weighted mean difference -49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47) is a different set of trials answering a narrower question, and it overlaps ours.
30782243Efficacy and safety of different doses of alirocumab in reducing low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels: a network meta-analysis. Pharmazie 2019.
A NETWORK estimate over sixteen studies rather than a direct pool over six, and its intervals are about forty points wide. Its alirocumab-versus-placebo relative effects run from -71 to -77, further from zero than our -54.8, and the abstract does not state the unit or the model well enough to say why.
31463238Safety and efficacy of alirocumab: A meta analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials. J Family Med Prim Care 2019.
It reports 'over 50%' LDL-C reduction without a pooled interval in its abstract, so it supplies a direction and a rough magnitude and no number to reconcile against.
29299849Lipid Management in Chronic Kidney Disease: Systematic Review of PCSK9 Targeting. Drugs 2019.
It reports no pooled estimate, but it is the record that independently confirms which ODYSSEY COMBO trial used which comparator -- see the comparator check.

Where the numbers differ, and why

Table 13. Where the numbers differ, and why
This reviewMean difference -54.72 percent (-60.62 to -48.82) in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24, k=8, random effects, REML. PREDICTION INTERVAL -71.18 to -38.26, which is the number to quote.
The published synthesis-49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47) over seven familial-hypercholesterolaemia trials of both PCSK9 antibodies; 'over 50%' over twelve alirocumab trials; -71 to -77 by dose in a sixteen-study network analysis.
Why they differDifferent eligible sets and different questions -- one drug or two, one population or several, direct pool or network. Nothing here shows either side in error on the numbers. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT IS NOT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN REVIEWS, IT IS THE SPREAD WITHIN OURS: eight trials running from -39.1 to -64.1, each with a tight interval of its own, I-squared near 90 per cent. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a twenty-five point range, and the prediction interval is the only honest summary of it.

How they were identified: PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/alirocumab-lipid/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 101 records matched and all 101 were read at abstract level.

Abstract

Question. In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo?1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 were searched; estimates were pooled under random with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE.2

Results. Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24: mean difference -54.7 (-60.6 to -48.8) across 8 trials; and heterogeneity was poorly (I-squared 90%).3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo? It pools 8 randomised trials, against placebo. The outcome pooled is Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24. Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- QUERY 1, NARROW (condition + drug) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: query.cond="hypercholesterolemia"; query.intr="alirocumab"; filter.advanced=AREA[StudyType]INTERVENTIONAL; pageSize=200; countTotal=true. It returned 54 record(s).1

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- QUERY 2, BROAD (intervention only) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: query.intr="alirocumab OR praluent OR SAR236553 OR REGN727"; filter.advanced=AREA[StudyType]INTERVENTIONAL; pageSize=400; countTotal=true. It returned 99 record(s).2

PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 8 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry.3

Methods — synthesis

For percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24, a random model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.2

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook), following Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome. 6 result-level assessments were made. A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.3

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.4

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14: Completing 'Summary of findings' tables and grading the certainty of the evidence. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons. 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.5

Refused: the claim that records were screened in duplicate -- and this topic OWES one rather than merely lacking one: No second independent screen was run for this topic. This is recorded as OWED rather than described: the remedy is to RUN one, and writing a duplicate-screening sentence without one would be the defect this whole exercise exists to prevent.6
Refused: the claim that the review methods were prespecified before data collection. THIS REFUSAL IS PERMANENT AND IS NOT A GAP TO BE FILLED. A protocol specified before data collection is a HISTORICAL FACT ABOUT THE PAST and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them. Eligibility criteria were derived POST HOC from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each. MECIR R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria PROVIDED THEY ARE DECLARED AS SUCH. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.7

Results

The pooled mean difference for percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24 was -54.7 (-60.6 to -48.8, 95% interval) across 8 trials, against placebo.1

The trials' results were poorly consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 90%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 61.4, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 58.4, on degrees of freedom 7. high2

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Every included trial reports this outcome with an effect estimate and an interval. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.3

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.4

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome.1

NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT OUR ACCESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TRIALS. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from SOME CONCERNS need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. SOME CONCERNS IS THEREFORE THE CEILING, NOT A FINDING. A trial rated SOME CONCERNS here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite. Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.2

A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.3

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons.1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

risk_of_bias -1 inconsistency -1 indirectness +0 imprecision +0 publication_bias +03

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D5 on 6 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step5
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24LOW8HIGHrisk of bias: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s) -- Result-level RoB 2 over 6 contributing result(s): NO_INFORMATION=6. NOT ONE reaches LOW -- D5 cannot, because no trial's statistical analysis plan is held, and D1 cannot, because allocation concealment is in neither the registration nor this object. 6 have at least one domain at NO INFORMATION. This is a limit on what we can reach, not a finding against the trials.; inconsistency: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- I-squared 88% over k = 8. Rated down. I-squared is one input and never the test -- P36 -- but at this magnitude with a small k the point estimates genuinely disperse.; indirectness: not rated down -- The contributing results share one endpoint definition, verified by reading each trial's registered text rather than by comparing names.; imprecision: not rated down -- k = 8 and the interval (-60.62 to -48.82) excludes the null. [RESTATED 2026-08-20 with the REML values; the original is beside this under reason_superseded_2026_08_20.] (reason superseded 2026 08 20: k = 8 and the interval (-60.23 to -49.42) excludes the null.); publication bias: not rated down -- k = 8. A funnel plot and Egger's test have no power below k = 10, so publication bias is UNDETECTED rather than ABSENT. Not rated down, and not reported as clean: an unreachable state is not a passing one.

Discussion

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the effect size is clinically meaningful. The pooled MD is -54.72 (95% CI -60.62 to -48.82) over 8 trials. Certainty is rated LOW. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. WHETHER A CHANGE OF THAT MAGNITUDE IS CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL IN THIS POPULATION IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT: NO FIELD ON THIS OBJECT RECORDS A THRESHOLD OF IMPORTANCE, AND NONE IS ASSUMED HERE.1

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the observed heterogeneity is clinically important. Across 8 trials, tau-squared 61.4414; every trial interval excludes no effect. WHETHER THAT DEGREE OF DISAGREEMENT MATTERS CLINICALLY -- WHETHER THE TRIALS ARE ANSWERING THE SAME QUESTION IN THE SAME PATIENTS -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.2

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- WHY this result differs from the published ones, mechanically or methodologically. This review pools -54.72 (95% CI -60.62 to -48.82) over 8 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled an outcome not recorded here. WHY THE TWO RESULTS DIFFER -- WHETHER BY POPULATION, OUTCOME DEFINITION, MODEL OR INCLUDED SET -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.3

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the evidence base is adequate to answer the question. The evidence base is 8 trials, assessed for risk of bias as NO_INFORMATION on 6 result(s). GRADE certainty is LOW. WHETHER THAT IS ENOUGH TO ANSWER THE QUESTION DEPENDS ON THE DECISION THE ANSWER IS FOR, WHICH IS NOT STATED ON THIS OBJECT, AND IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.4

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the search was broad enough. PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 8 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. WHETHER THAT IS BROAD ENOUGH FOR THE CLAIM THIS REVIEW MAKES IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.5

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- What further evidence would change the conclusion. Certainty was not rated down on any GRADE domain. WHAT FURTHER EVIDENCE WOULD CHANGE THE CONCLUSION IS A JUDGEMENT ABOUT A TRIAL NOBODY HAS RUN, AND IS THE AUTHOR'S.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/alirocumab-lipid/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 101 records matched and all 101 were read at abstract level.1

This review was compared against 4 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

Where our result differs from theirs: Different eligible sets and different questions -- one drug or two, one population or several, direct pool or network. Nothing here shows either side in error on the numbers. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT IS NOT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN REVIEWS, IT IS THE SPREAD WITHIN OURS: eight trials running from -39.1 to -64.1, each with a tight interval of its own, I-squared near 90 per cent. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a twenty-five point range, and the prediction interval is the only honest summary of it.3

Note on registration

Protocol status. Prespecified: False. A protocol specified before data collection is a HISTORICAL FACT ABOUT THE PAST and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.1

Eligibility criteria were derived POST HOC from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each.2

Authority: MECIR R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria PROVIDED THEY ARE DECLARED AS SUCH. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.3

NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.4

k3_corrected_fromk3 was 74 and background 18 before the placebo-name fix of 2026-08-19. The ODYSSEY registrations name the placebo arm's intervention 'Placebo (for alirocumab)', so a substring match reported the drug in BOTH arms and locate() returned background_or_coadministered on FIVE OF THIS OBJECT'S SIX INCLUDED TRIALS. A PLACEBO FOR X IS NOT X. Fixed by anchoring: a placebo declares itself at the START of its own name. 8.4% of intervention records to hand name the drug their placebo substitutes for, so this was an industry-wide convention rather than one registry's data entry.

The cell is named and kept at zero rather than deleted, because deleting it would make the gap this review had in its own evidence base unreadable from the finished page., what this says READ BY THE REMAINDER-DIAGNOSIS RULE (PAGE-STANDARD, 'Reading the remainder'): 34 of 81 fail a criterion, 21 are eligible with a different estimand, and 26 have not reported.
